  "concordance_metric": "area under the receiver–operator curve (AUC)",
  "concordance_value": 0.72,
  "n_pairs": 39,
  "n_animal_studies": null,
  "n_human_studies": 39,
  "species_results": [],
  "two_by_two": null,
  "sensitivity": 0.64,
  "specificity": 0.88,
  "ppv": null,
  "npv": null,
  "endpoints_animal": [
    "hERG current block potency (IC50)",
    "hERG safety margins (IC50/Cmax or IC50/free Cmax)"
  ],
  "endpoints_human": [
    "QTc prolongation (mean increase ≥ 5 ms)"
  ],
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "concordance_definition": "The study defined concordance by evaluating the performance of hERG safety margins in relation to clinically measured delayed repolarization. Receiver-operator curves (ROCs) were used, plotting sensitivity (true positive rate) against (1-specificity) (true negative rate). The area under the ROC curve (AUC) summarized diagnostic accuracy. Optimal performance was identified at the point closest to the upper-left corner of the ROC graph.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "IC50 values were not measured in a single central laboratory; experimental conditions were not standardized.",
    "Details of assay conditions were not always provided.",
    "Variability in bath exposures might not have been fully controlled.",
    "The possible role of electrophysiologically active metabolites in vivo was not considered.",
    "Effects of drugs on hERG channel trafficking to the sarcolemmal membrane were not considered.",
    "The number of drugs for which hERG block potency has been reported is relatively small.",
    "TQT studies are designed to detect small levels of QTc prolongation, and not all TQT studies followed the same protocol."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": null,
  "key_numbers": [
    "39 drugs compared for hERG block potency and clinical QTc prolongation.",
    "A hERG safety margin of 45 provided optimal overall performance linking safety margins to QTc prolongation.",
    "Sensitivity (true positive rate) = 0.64, specificity (true negative rate) = 0.88 at a safety margin of 45.",
    "Area under the receiver–operator curve (AUC) = 0.72, indicative of moderate overall concordance.",
    "QTc prolonging drugs are 5–7 times as likely to demonstrate low safety margins (1–30 range) compared to drugs that do not prolong QTc.",
    "Most (9/10) drugs eliciting essentially no hERG block at maximal concentrations demonstrated no QTc prolongation.",
    "A mean increase in baseline-corrected, time-matched, placebo-controlled, QTc interval of 5 ms is recognized as an indication of concern.",
    "Average plasma protein binding value of the 39 drugs was 74.7 ± 31.4 (s.d.).",
    "For 34 drugs, the average peak QTc prolongation with moxifloxacin was 11.14±2.82 ms.",
    "The optimal decision threshold for the free hERG safety margin was obtained with a decision threshold of ~45.",
    "Assay sensitivity was 0.69 and specificity was 0.81 for the standard dataset (n=29) at the optimal cut-off of 45.",
    "Assay sensitivity was 0.64 and specificity was 0.88 for the extended dataset (n=39) at the optimal cut-off of 45.",
    "The highest likelihood ratio of 7.14 is obtained using the free hERG safety margin range of 1–30.",
    "Drugs with safety margins ranging from 1 to 30 demonstrated moderately increased probability of QTc prolongation (88%)."
  ]
}
